info.desc: "Speaking in Tongues" is the fifth studio album by American rock band Talking Heads, released on June 1, 1983, by Sire Records. After their split with producer Brian Eno and a short hiatus, which allowed the individual members to pursue side projects, recording began in 1982. It became the band's commercial breakthrough and produced the band's sole US top-ten hit, "Burning Down the House". The album's tour was documented in Jonathan Demme's 1984 film Stop Making Sense, which generated a live album of the same name. The album also crossed over to the dance charts, where it peaked at number .

podcast.body: This album was self-produced by Talking Heads, with David Byrne steering the band towards a "commercially funky direction" after reportedly envying Tom Tom Club's success. The lineup was beefed up with seasoned black players including guitarist Alex Weir, percussionist Steve Scales, and synth player Bernie Worrell. Released in summer 1983, it was steeped in funk, R&B, and gospel, featuring bumping keyboards, stomping basslines, and call-and-response vocals on "Slippery People" with Nona Hendryx. It became Talking Heads' most commercially successful music to date, reaching number 15, going platinum, and generating their first and only Top 10 pop hit, "Burning Down the House." "The result was the most commercially successful talking heads music to date."
